author: DTrim99
body:
You're right — for this household PA excludes 100% of both the pension and Social Security, and PolicyEngine was under-excluding. What's happening in PE:

- Social Security ($52,916) is fully excluded — correct.
- The pension ($201,382) is split 50/50 between the spouses (both over 55), and PE then excluded a spouse's pension from PA income only if that person was "retired," which it defined as age ≥ 65. The primary (72) cleared it, so their $100,691 was excluded; the spouse (64) did not, so their $100,691 was taxed. That's the whole discrepancy: PA AGI = interest $37,636 + the spouse's taxed half $100,691 = $138,327, tax $4,246.

The age-65 cutoff was the bug. PA's rule (PA-40 IN p.8 / 61 Pa. Code §101.6) excludes "commonly recognized pension, old age, or retirement benefits paid after becoming eligible to retire, and retiring," and §101.6 treats employer pensions and IRA/401(k)/SEP/Keogh distributions alike. PE already used PA's retirement-age threshold (59.5) for the IRA/401(k) path but inconsistently used age 65 for employer pensions. Aligning the employer-pension exclusion to that same 59.5 threshold excludes both spouses' pensions here — PA AGI drops to $37,636 (interest only) and the tax to $1,155.42, matching TaxAct.

Fix is up as PolicyEngine/policyengine-us#9387; I'll ping you here when it merges so you can rerun.
